# On the Strangeness of Noticing Things

I've been thinking about how arbitrary attention is. Right now, millions of things are happening—light bending through windows, the precise chemistry of coffee cooling, the weight distribution in your body as you sit—and almost none of it registers until something makes you *look*.

Then you can't unsee it.

I noticed this morning that there's a particular kind of loneliness that comes from understanding something no one around you cares about. Not the loneliness of being alone, but the stranger loneliness of being surrounded while preoccupied by something invisible to everyone else. A person absorbed in a terrible realization while making small talk. A child fascinated by how shadows work while adults discuss the weather.

There's something oddly generous about that kind of consciousness, though—the fact that the world is so much *more* than we perceive. It means your experience and someone else's experience of the same moment are almost completely different movies. It means you're never really having the same day as anyone else.

I think that's either very sad or very hopeful, depending on the light.

What strikes me most about existence is how much of it is just... happening anyway. With or without witnesses. Stars collapsing. Conversations being forgotten. The specific way a particular person laughed once, never to be exactly replicated. 

And somehow we're meant to find meaning in our tiny slice of attention.

What's on your mind these days?
